3	from __future__ import annotations
4	
5	import contextlib
6	import json
7	import os
8	import tempfile
9	import threading
10	from typing import Any
11	
12	from ._jsonio import strict_loads
13	
14	__all__ = ["register"]
15	
16	_VERSION = 1
17	_OFFER_FIELDS = ("resource_id", "region", "capacity_wh",
18	                 "unit_cost", "carbon_intensity")
19	_REQUIRED_FIELDS = frozenset(_OFFER_FIELDS)
20	_ROOT_FIELDS = ("version", "offers", "idempotency")
21	
22	
23	class _Store:
24	    def __init__(self, realpath: str) -> None:
25	        self.realpath = realpath
26	        self.lock = threading.Lock()
27	
28	
29	_stores_lock = threading.Lock()
30	_stores: dict[str, _Store] = {}
31	
32	
33	def _get_store(path: str) -> _Store:
34	    realpath = os.path.realpath(path)
35	    with _stores_lock:
36	        store = _stores.get(realpath)
37	        if store is None:
38	            store = _Store(realpath)
39	            _stores[realpath] = store
40	        return store
41	
42	
43	def _is_plain_int(value: object) -> bool:
44	    # bool is a subclass of int and must be rejected.
45	    return isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool)
46	
47	
48	def _normalize_offer(
49	    offer: object,
50	) -> tuple[str, str, int, int, int]:
51	    if not isinstance(offer, dict) or set(offer.keys()) != _REQUIRED_FIELDS:
52	        raise ValueError("offer must be an object with exactly resource_id, "
53	                         "region, capacity_wh, unit_cost and carbon_intensity")
54	
55	    resource_id = offer["resource_id"]
56	    if not isinstance(resource_id, str) or not resource_id:
57	        raise ValueError("resource_id must be a non-empty string")
58	
59	    region = offer["region"]
60	    if not isinstance(region, str) or not region:
61	        raise ValueError("region must be a non-empty string")
62	
63	    capacity_wh = offer["capacity_wh"]
64	    if not _is_plain_int(capacity_wh) or capacity_wh <= 0:
65	        raise ValueError("capacity_wh must be a non-boolean positive integer")
66	
67	    unit_cost = offer["unit_cost"]
68	    if not _is_plain_int(unit_cost) or unit_cost < 0:
69	        raise ValueError("unit_cost must be a non-boolean non-negative integer")
70	
71	    carbon_intensity = offer["carbon_intensity"]
72	    if not _is_plain_int(carbon_intensity) or carbon_intensity < 0:
73	        raise ValueError("carbon_intensity must be a non-boolean "
74	                         "non-negative integer")
75	
76	    return resource_id, region, capacity_wh, unit_cost, carbon_intensity
77	
78	
79	def _validate_structure(
80	    data: object,
81	) -> tuple[dict[str, dict[str, Any]], dict[str, dict[str, str]]]:
82	    if not isinstance(data, dict) or set(data.keys()) != set(_ROOT_FIELDS):
83	        raise ValueError("registry root must be an object with keys "
84	                         "version, offers and idempotency")
85	
86	    version = data["version"]
87	    if not _is_plain_int(version) or version != _VERSION:
88	        raise ValueError("unsupported registry version")
89	
90	    offers_raw = data["offers"]
91	    idempotency_raw = data["idempotency"]
92	    if not isinstance(offers_raw, dict) or not isinstance(idempotency_raw, dict):
93	        raise ValueError("offers and idempotency must be objects")
94	
95	    offers: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
96	    for name, record in offers_raw.items():
97	        if not isinstance(name, str) or not name:
98	            raise ValueError("resource ids must be non-empty strings")
99	        if not isinstance(record, dict) or set(record.keys()) != _REQUIRED_FIELDS:
100	            raise ValueError("offer record has invalid fields")
101	        if record["resource_id"] != name:
102	            raise ValueError("offer record id does not match its key")
103	        if not isinstance(record["region"], str) or not record["region"]:
104	            raise ValueError("region must be a non-empty string")
105	        if (not _is_plain_int(record["capacity_wh"])
106	                or record["capacity_wh"] <= 0):
107	            raise ValueError("invalid capacity_wh")
108	        if not _is_plain_int(record["unit_cost"]) or record["unit_cost"] < 0:
109	            raise ValueError("invalid unit_cost")
110	        if (not _is_plain_int(record["carbon_intensity"])
111	                or record["carbon_intensity"] < 0):
112	            raise ValueError("invalid carbon_intensity")
113	        # Rebuild in canonical field order so that replays and rewrites of
114	        # records stored out of order still follow _OFFER_FIELDS.
115	        offers[name] = {field: record[field] for field in _OFFER_FIELDS}
116	
117	    idempotency: dict[str, dict[str, str]] = {}
118	    referenced: set[str] = set()
119	    for key, entry in idempotency_raw.items():
120	        if not isinstance(key, str) or not key:
121	            raise ValueError("idempotency keys must be non-empty strings")
122	        if not isinstance(entry, dict) or set(entry.keys()) != {"resource_id"}:
123	            raise ValueError("idempotency entry must be a resource_id object")
124	        resource_id = entry["resource_id"]
125	        if not isinstance(resource_id, str) or not resource_id \
126	                or resource_id not in offers:
127	            raise ValueError("idempotency entry must reference a "
128	                             "registered offer")
129	        if resource_id in referenced:
130	            raise ValueError("offer registered under more than one "
131	                             "idempotency key")
132	        referenced.add(resource_id)
133	        idempotency[key] = {"resource_id": resource_id}
134	
135	    return offers, idempotency
136

138	def _load(
139	    realpath: str,
140	) -> tuple[dict[str, dict[str, Any]], dict[str, dict[str, str]]]:
141	    try:
142	        with open(realpath, encoding="utf-8") as handle:
143	            text = handle.read()
144	    except FileNotFoundError:
145	        return {}, {}
146	
147	    try:

149	    except ValueError as exc:

190	    offer: dict[str, object],
191	    idempotency_key: str,
192	) -> tuple[dict[str, object], bool]:
193	    """Register a capacity offer idempotently as compact UTF-8 JSON.
194	
195	    Returns ``(record, created)`` where ``record`` carries resource_id,
196	    region, capacity_wh, unit_cost (micro-units per Wh) and carbon_intensity
197	    (g/kWh); ``created`` is ``True`` for a new registration and ``False``
198	    when the idempotency key replays an identical offer.
199	    """
200	    if not isinstance(path, str):
201	        raise ValueError("path must be a string")
202	    if not isinstance(idempotency_key, str) or not idempotency_key:
203	        raise ValueError("idempotency_key must be a non-empty string")
204	    resource_id, region, capacity_wh, unit_cost, carbon_intensity = \
205	        _normalize_offer(offer)
206	
207	    store = _get_store(path)
208	    with store.lock:
209	        offers, idempotency = _load(store.realpath)
210	        record: dict[str, object] = {
211	            "resource_id": resource_id,
212	            "region": region,
213	            "capacity_wh": capacity_wh,
214	            "unit_cost": unit_cost,
215	            "carbon_intensity": carbon_intensity,
216	        }
217	
218	        existing_entry = idempotency.get(idempotency_key)
219	        if existing_entry is not None:
220	            existing = offers[existing_entry["resource_id"]]
221	            if existing != record:
222	                raise ValueError("idempotency key was already used with a "
223	                                 "different offer")
224	            return dict(existing), False
225	
226	        if resource_id in offers:
227	            raise ValueError("resource_id is already registered under "
228	                             "another idempotency key")
229	
230	        offers[resource_id] = record
231	        idempotency[idempotency_key] = {"resource_id": resource_id}
232	        _atomic_write(store.realpath, offers, idempotency)
233	        return dict(record), True

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import threading
import unittest
from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory

from carbon_market import offers as offers_module
from carbon_market.offers import register


def _offer(resource_id: str = "r-1", **overrides: object) -> dict[str, object]:
    offer: dict[str, object] = {
        "resource_id": resource_id,
        "region": "eu-north",
        "capacity_wh": 250,
        "unit_cost": 1000,
        "carbon_intensity": 42,
    }
    offer.update(overrides)
    return offer


class RegisterTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self) -> None:
        self.tmp = TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(self.tmp.cleanup)
        self.path = os.path.join(self.tmp.name, "registry.json")

    def test_creates_file_and_returns_record(self) -> None:
        record, created = register(self.path, _offer(), "key-1")
        self.assertTrue(created)
        self.assertEqual(record, {
            "resource_id": "r-1",
            "region": "eu-north",
            "capacity_wh": 250,
            "unit_cost": 1000,
            "carbon_intensity": 42,
        })
        self.assertEqual(list(record.keys()),
                         ["resource_id", "region", "capacity_wh",
                          "unit_cost", "carbon_intensity"])
        self.assertTrue(os.path.exists(self.path))
        raw = Path(self.path).read_bytes()
        self.assertTrue(raw.endswith(b"\n"))
        self.assertFalse(raw.endswith(b"\n\n"))
        data = json.loads(raw)
        self.assertEqual(list(data.keys()), ["version", "offers", "idempotency"])
        self.assertEqual(data["version"], 1)
        self.assertEqual(list(data["offers"].keys()), ["r-1"])
        self.assertEqual(list(data["offers"]["r-1"].keys()),
                         ["resource_id", "region", "capacity_wh",
                          "unit_cost", "carbon_intensity"])
        self.assertEqual(data["idempotency"],
                         {"key-1": {"resource_id": "r-1"}})

    def test_compact_utf8_json(self) -> None:
        register(self.path, _offer(resource_id="r-中", region="北"), "键")
        raw = Path(self.path).read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        self.assertIn("r-中", raw)
        self.assertIn("北", raw)
        self.assertIn("键", raw)
        self.assertNotIn(" ", raw.split("\n", 1)[0])

    def test_idempotent_replay(self) -> None:
        first, created_first = register(self.path, _offer(), "key")
        second, created_second = register(self.path, _offer(), "key")
        self.assertTrue(created_first)
        self.assertFalse(created_second)
        self.assertEqual(first, second)
        data = json.loads(Path(self.path).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))

                    errors.append(exc)

            threads = [threading.Thread(target=worker, args=(path, i))
                       for i, path in enumerate(paths * 20)]

1	"""Persistence infrastructure shared by the persistent ledgers.
2	
3	Every persistent ledger -- the dispatch, execution and completion
4	ledgers, the live market inputs (the resource-supply registry and the
5	signal ledger), and the audit, audit-proof, jobs, market, rebalance,
6	execution-sync, migration-batch, recover-all and signal-ingest ledgers
7	-- protects its file the same way: one in-process mutex per resolved
8	real path, a companion ``.lock`` file carrying ``flock``
9	shared/exclusive locks across processes, and a synced same-directory
10	temporary file atomically renamed over the ledger with its directory
11	fsynced and the pre-call bytes restored on failure.
12	
13	This module holds exactly that shared machinery:
14	
15	* :class:`Store` and :func:`get_store` -- the per-real-path mutex
16	  registry;
17	* :func:`file_lock` -- the companion-lock flock;
18	* :func:`is_plain_int` and :func:`check_sorted_keys` -- the small input
19	  checks every ledger repeats;
20	* :func:`load_canonical` -- read, decode, validate and re-canonicalize
21	  one ledger, preserving each caller's missing-file handling and error
22	  wording;
23	* :func:`fsync_directory`, :func:`commit_file` -- the durable atomic
24	  commit and its rollback.
25	
26	It is an internal module: it defines no business entry point, owns no
27	ledger format and opens no file that callers did not name.
28	"""
29	
30	from __future__ import annotations
31	
32	import contextlib
33	import fcntl
34	import os
35	import tempfile
36	import threading
37	from typing import Any, Callable, Iterator, TypeVar
38	
39	from ._jsonio import finite_loads
40	
41	__all__ = [
42	    "Store", "get_store", "file_lock", "is_plain_int", "check_sorted_keys",
43	    "load_canonical", "fsync_directory", "commit_file",
44	]
45	
46	_LOCK_SUFFIX = ".lock"
47	
48	_T = TypeVar("_T")
49	
50	
51	class Store:
52	    """The in-process mutex bound to one resolved ledger path.
53	
54	    Equivalent real paths -- one path given through a symlink and
55	    another given directly -- resolve to one store, so threads in this
56	    process serialize on one lock while the companion flock serializes
57	    against other processes.
58	    """
59	
60	    def __init__(self, realpath: str) -> None:
61	        self.realpath = realpath
62	        self.lock = threading.Lock()
63	
64	
65	_stores_lock = threading.Lock()
66	_stores: dict[str, Store] = {}
67	
68	
69	def get_store(path: str) -> Store:
70	    realpath = os.path.realpath(path)
71	    with _stores_lock:
72	        store = _stores.get(realpath)
73	        if store is None:
74	            store = Store(realpath)
75	            _stores[realpath] = store
76	        return store
77	
78	
79	def is_plain_int(value: object) -> bool:
80	    # bool is a subclass of int and must be rejected.
81	    return isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool)
82	
83	
84	@contextlib.contextmanager
85	def file_lock(realpath: str, *, shared: bool = False) -> Iterator[None]:
86	    # The companion lock file is never unlinked and an flock is released
87	    # by the kernel on process exit, so equivalent real paths share one
88	    # lock across threads and processes -- and across modules, since
89	    # every layer uses the same suffix for the same file.
90	    lock_path = realpath + _LOCK_SUFFIX
91	    fd = os.open(lock_path, os.O_CREAT | os.O_RDWR, 0o666)
92	    try:
93	        fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_SH if shared else fcntl.LOCK_EX)
94	        try:
95	            yield
96	        finally:
97	            fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_UN)
98	    finally:
99	        os.close(fd)
100	
101	
102	def check_sorted_keys(mapping: dict[Any, Any], label: str) -> None:
103	    keys = list(mapping)
104	    if keys != sorted(keys):
105	        raise ValueError(f"{label} must be ordered by key code point")
106	
107	
108	def load_canonical(
109	    realpath: str,
110	    label: str,
111	    validate: Callable[[object], _T],
112	    canonical: Callable[[_T], bytes],
113	) -> tuple[_T | None, bytes | None]:
114	    """Read and verify one canonical lifecycle ledger.
115	
116	    ``label`` is the ledger name used in error wording (e.g.
117	    ``"dispatch ledger"``). ``validate`` turns the decoded JSON into the
118	    caller's normalized section tuple/object, raising ``ValueError`` on
119	    any structural problem, and ``canonical`` renders it back to the
120	    exact on-disk form.
121	
122	    A missing file returns ``(None, None)``: callers keep their own
123	    missing-file policy (empty initial state, ``FileNotFoundError`` or
124	    ``KeyError``). Every other problem raises ``ValueError`` with the
125	    same wording the ledgers carried before the infrastructure was
126	    shared, and the re-rendered bytes must match the file byte for byte.
127	    """
128	    try:
129	        with open(realpath, "rb") as handle:
130	            raw = handle.read()
131	    except FileNotFoundError:
132	        return None, None
133	    try:
134	        text = raw.decode("utf-8")
135	    except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
136	        raise ValueError(
137	            f"{label} {realpath!r} is not valid UTF-8") from exc
138	    try:
139	        # Negative-zero and non-finite literals are format errors.
140	        data = finite_loads(text)
141	    except ValueError as exc:
142	        raise ValueError(
143	            f"{label} {realpath!r} is not valid JSON") from exc
144	    sections = validate(data)
145	    # The ledger is accepted only in canonical compact form with a
146	    # single trailing newline.
147	    if raw != canonical(sections):
148	        raise ValueError(
149	            f"{label} {realpath!r} is not in canonical compact form")
150	    return sections, raw

153	def fsync_directory(directory: str) -> None:
154	    dir_fd = os.open(directory, os.O_RDONLY)
155	    try:
156	        os.fsync(dir_fd)
157	    finally:
158	        os.close(dir_fd)
159

161	def rollback_file(
162	    realpath: str,
163	    directory: str,
164	    old_bytes: bytes | None,
165	    first: BaseException,
166	    *,
167	    prefix: str = ".restore-",
168	    fsync_dir: Callable[[str], None] | None = None,
169	) -> None:
170	    # Restore the exact pre-call bytes while the exclusive lock is held,
171	    # or remove a ledger that did not exist beforehand, then sync the
172	    # directory. A failed recovery chains after the original error. The
173	    # directory-sync call is injectable so each ledger keeps its own
174	    # module-level fault-injection seam.
175	    if fsync_dir is None:
176	        fsync_dir = fsync_directory
177	    try:
178	        if old_bytes is None:
179	            try:
180	                os.unlink(realpath)
181	            except FileNotFoundError:
182	                pass
183	        else:
184	            fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(
185	                dir=directory, prefix=prefix, suffix=".tmp")
186	            try:
187	                with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as handle:
188	                    handle.write(old_bytes)
189	                    handle.flush()
190	                    os.fsync(handle.fileno())
191	                os.replace(tmp_path, realpath)
192	            except BaseException:
193	                with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
194	                    os.unlink(tmp_path)

196	        fsync_dir(directory)
197	    except OSError as recovery:
198	        raise recovery from first

201	def commit_file(
202	    realpath: str,
203	    payload: bytes,
204	    old_bytes: bytes | None,
205	    *,
206	    prefix: str = ".",
207	    fsync_dir: Callable[[str], None] | None = None,
208	) -> None:
209	    """Publish ``payload`` over ``realpath`` as one durable commit.
210	
211	    The payload is fully written to a same-directory temporary file and
212	    fsynced, then atomically replaces the ledger and the directory is
213	    fsynced. A failure before the replace leaves the pre-call bytes (or
214	    absence) untouched; a failure while syncing the directory after the
215	    replace restores the original bytes -- or removes a ledger that did
216	    not exist beforehand -- and chains any recovery failure after the
217	    original error. Concurrent readers therefore observe only the
218	    complete old or the complete new version.

221	    its own module-level function to keep its fault-injection seam.
222	    """

"""Persistence infrastructure shared by the persistent ledgers.

Every persistent ledger -- the dispatch, execution and completion
ledgers, the live market inputs (the resource-supply registry and the
signal ledger), and the audit, audit-proof, jobs, market, rebalance,
execution-sync, migration-batch, recover-all and signal-ingest ledgers
-- protects its file the same way: one in-process mutex per resolved
real path, a companion ``.lock`` file carrying ``flock``
shared/exclusive locks across processes, and a synced same-directory
temporary file atomically renamed over the ledger with its directory
fsynced and the pre-call bytes restored on failure.

This module holds exactly that shared machinery:

* :class:`Store` and :func:`get_store` -- the per-real-path mutex
  registry;
* :func:`file_lock` -- the companion-lock flock;
* :func:`is_plain_int` and :func:`check_sorted_keys` -- the small input
  checks every ledger repeats;
* :func:`load_canonical` -- read, decode, validate and re-canonicalize
  one ledger, preserving each caller's missing-file handling and error
  wording;
* :func:`fsync_directory`, :func:`commit_file` -- the durable atomic
  commit and its rollback.

It is an internal module: it defines no business entry point, owns no
ledger format and opens no file that callers did not name.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import contextlib
import fcntl
import os
import tempfile
import threading
from typing import Any, Callable, Iterator, TypeVar

from ._jsonio import finite_loads

__all__ = [
    "Store", "get_store", "file_lock", "is_plain_int", "check_sorted_keys",
    "load_canonical", "fsync_directory", "commit_file",
]

_LOCK_SUFFIX = ".lock"

_T = TypeVar("_T")


class Store:
    """The in-process mutex bound to one resolved ledger path.

    Equivalent real paths -- one path given through a symlink and
    another given directly -- resolve to one store, so threads in this
    process serialize on one lock while the companion flock serializes
    against other processes.
    """

    def __init__(self, realpath: str) -> None:
        self.realpath = realpath
        self.lock = threading.Lock()


_stores_lock = threading.Lock()
_stores: dict[str, Store] = {}


def get_store(path: str) -> Store:
    realpath = os.path.realpath(path)
    with _stores_lock:
        store = _stores.get(realpath)
        if store is None:
            store = Store(realpath)
            _stores[realpath] = store
        return store


def is_plain_int(value: object) -> bool:
    # bool is a subclass of int and must be rejected.
    return isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool)


@contextlib.contextmanager
def file_lock(realpath: str, *, shared: bool = False) -> Iterator[None]:
    # The companion lock file is never unlinked and an flock is released
    # by the kernel on process exit, so equivalent real paths share one
    # lock across threads and processes -- and across modules, since
    # every layer uses the same suffix for the same file.
    lock_path = realpath + _LOCK_SUFFIX
    fd = os.open(lock_path, os.O_CREAT | os.O_RDWR, 0o666)
    try:
        fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_SH if shared else fcntl.LOCK_EX)
        try:
            yield
        finally:
            fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_UN)
    finally:
        os.close(fd)


def check_sorted_keys(mapping: dict[Any, Any], label: str) -> None:
    keys = list(mapping)
    if keys != sorted(keys):
        raise ValueError(f"{label} must be ordered by key code point")


def load_canonical(
    realpath: str,
    label: str,
    validate: Callable[[object], _T],
    canonical: Callable[[_T], bytes],
) -> tuple[_T | None, bytes | None]:
    """Read and verify one canonical lifecycle ledger.

    ``label`` is the ledger name used in error wording (e.g.
    ``"dispatch ledger"``). ``validate`` turns the decoded JSON into the
    caller's normalized section tuple/object, raising ``ValueError`` on
    any structural problem, and ``canonical`` renders it back to the
    exact on-disk form.

    A missing file returns ``(None, None)``: callers keep their own
    missing-file policy (empty initial state, ``FileNotFoundError`` or
    ``KeyError``). Every other problem raises ``ValueError`` with the
    same wording the ledgers carried before the infrastructure was
    shared, and the re-rendered bytes must match the file byte for byte.
    """
    try:
        with open(realpath, "rb") as handle:
            raw = handle.read()
    except FileNotFoundError:
        return None, None
    try:
        text = raw.decode("utf-8")
    except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
        raise ValueError(
            f"{label} {realpath!r} is not valid UTF-8") from exc
    try:
        # Negative-zero and non-finite literals are format errors.
        data = finite_loads(text)
    except ValueError as exc:
        raise ValueError(
            f"{label} {realpath!r} is not valid JSON") from exc
    sections = validate(data)
    # The ledger is accepted only in canonical compact form with a
    # single trailing newline.
    if raw != canonical(sections):
        raise ValueError(
            f"{label} {realpath!r} is not in canonical compact form")
    return sections, raw


def fsync_directory(directory: str) -> None:
    dir_fd = os.open(directory, os.O_RDONLY)
    try:
        os.fsync(dir_fd)
    finally:
        os.close(dir_fd)


def rollback_file(
    realpath: str,
    directory: str,
    old_bytes: bytes | None,
    first: BaseException,
    *,
    prefix: str = ".restore-",
    fsync_dir: Callable[[str], None] | None = None,
) -> None:
    # Restore the exact pre-call bytes while the exclusive lock is held,
    # or remove a ledger that did not exist beforehand, then sync the
    # directory. A failed recovery chains after the original error. The
    # directory-sync call is injectable so each ledger keeps its own
    # module-level fault-injection seam.
    if fsync_dir is None:
        fsync_dir = fsync_directory
    try:
        if old_bytes is None:
            try:
                os.unlink(realpath)
            except FileNotFoundError:
                pass
        else:
            fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(
                dir=directory, prefix=prefix, suffix=".tmp")
            try:
                with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as handle:
                    handle.write(old_bytes)
                    handle.flush()
                    os.fsync(handle.fileno())
                os.replace(tmp_path, realpath)
            except BaseException:
                with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
                    os.unlink(tmp_path)
                raise
        fsync_dir(directory)
    except OSError as recovery:
        raise recovery from first


def commit_file(
    realpath: str,
    payload: bytes,
    old_bytes: bytes | None,
    *,
    prefix: str = ".",
    fsync_dir: Callable[[str], None] | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Publish ``payload`` over ``realpath`` as one durable commit.

    The payload is fully written to a same-directory temporary file and
    fsynced, then atomically replaces the ledger and the directory is
    fsynced. A failure before the replace leaves the pre-call bytes (or
    absence) untouched; a failure while syncing the directory after the
    replace restores the original bytes -- or removes a ledger that did
    not exist beforehand -- and chains any recovery failure after the
    original error. Concurrent readers therefore observe only the
    complete old or the complete new version.

    ``fsync_dir`` defaults to :func:`fsync_directory`; a caller passes
    its own module-level function to keep its fault-injection seam.
    """
    # One durable commit for the record, the idempotency binding and the
    # audit event: synced same-directory temporary, atomic replace and a
    # directory fsync, restoring the pre-call bytes on any failure.
    if fsync_dir is None:
        fsync_dir = fsync_directory
    directory = os.path.dirname(realpath) or "."
    fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(
        dir=directory, prefix=prefix, suffix=".tmp")
    try:
        with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as handle:
            handle.write(payload)
            handle.flush()
            os.fsync(handle.fileno())
        os.replace(tmp_path, realpath)
    except BaseException:
        with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
            os.unlink(tmp_path)
        raise
    try:
        fsync_dir(directory)
    except BaseException as first:
        rollback_file(realpath, directory, old_bytes, first,
                      prefix=prefix + "restore-", fsync_dir=fsync_dir)
        raise

        raise ValueError("registry root must be an object with keys "
                         "version, jobs and idempotency")

    version = data["version"]
    if not _is_plain_int(version) or version != _VERSION:
        raise ValueError("unsupported registry version")

    jobs_raw = data["jobs"]
    idempotency_raw = data["idempotency"]
    if not isinstance(jobs_raw, dict) or not isinstance(idempotency_raw, dict):
        raise ValueError("jobs and idempotency must be objects")

    jobs: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
    for name, record in jobs_raw.items():
        if not isinstance(name, str) or not name:
            raise ValueError("job ids must be non-empty strings")
        if not isinstance(record, dict) or set(record.keys()) != set(_JOB_FIELDS):
            raise ValueError("job record has invalid fields")
        if record["job_id"] != name:
            raise ValueError("job record id does not match its key")
        if not isinstance(record["job_id"], str):
            raise ValueError("job_id must be a string")
        if not _is_plain_int(record["deadline"]) or record["deadline"] < 0:
            raise ValueError("invalid deadline")
        if not _is_plain_int(record["energy_wh"]) or record["energy_wh"] <= 0:
            raise ValueError("invalid energy_wh")
        _validate_regions(record["residency_regions"])
        if record["state"] != _STATE:
            raise ValueError("invalid job state")
        jobs[name] = dict(record)

    idempotency: dict[str, str] = {}
    referenced: set[str] = set()
    for key, job_id in idempotency_raw.items():
        if not isinstance(key, str) or not key:
            raise ValueError("idempotency keys must be non-empty strings")
        if not isinstance(job_id, str) or not job_id or job_id not in jobs:
            raise ValueError("idempotency entry must reference a registered job")
        if job_id in referenced:
            raise ValueError("job registered under more than one idempotency key")
        referenced.add(job_id)
        idempotency[key] = job_id

    return jobs, idempotency


def _load(realpath: str) -> tuple[dict[str, dict[str, Any]], dict[str, str]]:
    try:
        with open(realpath, encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            text = handle.read()
    except FileNotFoundError:
        return {}, {}

    try:
        data = strict_loads(text)
    except ValueError as exc:
        raise ValueError(f"registry file {realpath!r} is not valid JSON") from exc
    return _validate_structure(data)


def _atomic_write(
    realpath: str,
    jobs: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
    idempotency: dict[str, str],
) -> None:
    payload = {
        "version": _VERSION,
        "jobs": {name: jobs[name] for name in sorted(jobs)},
        "idempotency": {key: idempotency[key] for key in sorted(idempotency)},
    }
    text = json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"),
                      allow_nan=False) + "\n"

    directory = os.path.dirname(realpath) or "."
    fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=directory, prefix=".jobs-", suffix=".tmp")
    try:
        with os.fdopen(fd, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as handle:
            handle.write(text)
            handle.flush()
            os.fsync(handle.fileno())
        os.replace(tmp_path, realpath)
    except BaseException:
        with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
            os.unlink(tmp_path)
        raise

    dir_fd = os.open(directory, os.O_RDONLY)
    try:
        os.fsync(dir_fd)
    finally:
        os.close(dir_fd)


def register(
    path: str,
    job: dict[str, object],
    idempotency_key: str,
) -> tuple[dict[str, object], bool]:
    """Register a job idempotently, persisting it as compact UTF-8 JSON.

    Returns ``(record, created)`` where ``record`` carries job_id, deadline,
    energy_wh, residency_regions (sorted by code point) and ``state`` set to
    ``"queued"``; ``created`` is ``True`` for a new registration and ``False``
    when the idempotency key replays an identical, normalized job.
    """
    if not isinstance(path, str):
        raise ValueError("path must be a string")
    if not isinstance(idempotency_key, str) or not idempotency_key:
        raise ValueError("idempotency_key must be a non-empty string")
    job_id, deadline, energy_wh, regions = _normalize_job(job)

    store = _get_store(path)
    with store.lock:
        jobs, idempotency = _load(store.realpath)
        record: dict[str, object] = {
            "job_id": job_id,
            "deadline": deadline,
            "energy_wh": energy_wh,
            "residency_regions": regions,
            "state": _STATE,
        }

        existing_id = idempotency.get(idempotency_key)
        if existing_id is not None:
            existing = jobs[existing_id]
            if existing != record:
                raise ValueError("idempotency key was already used with a "
                                 "different job")
            return dict(existing), False

        if job_id in jobs:
            raise ValueError("job_id is already registered under another "
                             "idempotency key")

        jobs[job_id] = record
        idempotency[idempotency_key] = job_id
        _atomic_write(store.realpath, jobs, idempotency)
        return dict(record), True

def _serialize_submit_file(
    jobs: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
    idempotency: dict[str, str],
    events: dict[str, dict[str, str]],
) -> bytes:
    # Compact UTF-8 JSON, non-ASCII written through, each section's
    # primary keys in code-point order, terminated by exactly one newline.
    payload = {
        "version": _SUBMIT_VERSION,
        "jobs": {name: jobs[name] for name in sorted(jobs)},
        "idempotency": {key: idempotency[key] for key in sorted(idempotency)},
        "audit": {key: events[key] for key in sorted(events)},
    }
    text = json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"),
                      allow_nan=False) + "\n"
    return text.encode("utf-8")


def _rollback_submit_file(realpath: str, directory: str,
                          old_bytes: bytes | None,
                          first: BaseException) -> None:
    # Restore the exact pre-call bytes while the exclusive lock is held:
    # stage them back over the replaced file, or remove a file that did
    # not exist beforehand, then sync the directory. A failed recovery
    # surfaces chained after the original error.
    try:
        if old_bytes is None:
            try:
                os.unlink(realpath)
            except FileNotFoundError:
                pass
        else:
            fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(
                dir=directory, prefix=".jobs-restore-", suffix=".tmp")
            try:
                with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as handle:
                    handle.write(old_bytes)
                    handle.flush()
                    os.fsync(handle.fileno())
                os.replace(tmp_path, realpath)
            except BaseException:
                with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
                    os.unlink(tmp_path)
                raise
        _fsync_directory(directory)
    except OSError as recovery:
        raise recovery from first


def _fsync_directory(directory: str) -> None:
    dir_fd = os.open(directory, os.O_RDONLY)
    try:
        os.fsync(dir_fd)
    finally:
        os.close(dir_fd)


def _commit_submit_file(realpath: str, payload: bytes,
                        old_bytes: bytes | None) -> None:
    # One durable commit for jobs, the idempotency map and the audit
    # event: same-directory temporary, fsync, atomic replace and a
    # directory fsync. Any failure after the replace restores the
    # pre-call bytes, so an unsuccessful submit leaves the original file
    # byte-for-byte.
    directory = os.path.dirname(realpath) or "."
    fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(
        dir=directory, prefix=".jobs-submit-", suffix=".tmp")
    try:
        with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as handle:
            handle.write(payload)
            handle.flush()
            os.fsync(handle.fileno())
        os.replace(tmp_path, realpath)
    except BaseException as first:
        with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
            os.unlink(tmp_path)
        raise
    try:
        _fsync_directory(directory)
    except BaseException as first:
        _rollback_submit_file(realpath, directory, old_bytes, first)
        raise


def submit(path: str, job: dict[str, object], idempotency_key: str
           ) -> tuple[dict[str, object], bool]:
    """Persistently accept a complete scheduling-constraint job.

    ``path`` and ``idempotency_key`` must be non-empty strings. The job
    must be an object with exactly the seven top-level fields job_id,
    work, deadline, regions, residency, max_cost and carbon_cap: a
    non-empty id, a positive work amount, non-negative deadline,
    max_cost and carbon_cap (booleans rejected), and two non-empty lists
    of distinct non-empty region strings, residency a subset of regions.
    Any deviation raises ``ValueError`` before the file is touched.

    A first acceptance saves the canonical job -- both region lists
    sorted by code point, state ``"queued"`` -- together with the
    idempotency binding and a submit audit event carrying the key, the
    job id and the queued result, all three in one durable commit, and
    returns ``(record, True)``. Replaying the same key with an
    equivalent job returns the stored record with ``False`` without
    adding an event or rewriting the file; the same key with a different
    job, an already accepted job id under another key, or any constraint
    mismatch raises ``ValueError`` and preserves the original bytes.

    A missing parent directory raises ``FileNotFoundError``; an invalid
    existing file (encoding, JSON, negative-zero or non-finite numbers,
    version, structure, ordering or references) raises ``ValueError``;
    any other locking or I/O failure raises ``OSError``. Calls serialize
    across threads and processes per resolved real path.
    """
    if not isinstance(path, str) or not path:
        raise ValueError("path must be a non-empty string")
    if not isinstance(idempotency_key, str) or not idempotency_key:
        raise ValueError("idempotency_key must be a non-empty string")
    record = _normalize_submit_job(job)
    job_id = record["job_id"]

    store = _get_store(path)
    with store.lock:
        # Opening the companion lock in a missing directory surfaces as
        # FileNotFoundError before the data file is created.
        with _process_lock(store.realpath):
            jobs, idempotency, events, old_bytes = _load_submit_file(
                store.realpath)

            existing_id = idempotency.get(idempotency_key)
            if existing_id is not None:
                existing = jobs[existing_id]
                if existing != record:
                    raise ValueError("idempotency key was already used with "
                                     "a different job")
                return dict(existing), False

            if job_id in jobs:
                raise ValueError("job_id is already accepted under another "
                                 "idempotency key")

            jobs[job_id] = record
            idempotency[idempotency_key] = job_id
            events[idempotency_key] = {
                "key": idempotency_key,
                "job_id": job_id,
                "result": _STATE,
            }
            _commit_submit_file(
                store.realpath,
                _serialize_submit_file(jobs, idempotency, events), old_bytes)
            return dict(record), True


def get(path: str, job_id: str) -> dict[str, object]:
    """Return a read-only copy of the accepted job stored under ``job_id``.

    ``path`` and ``job_id`` must be non-empty strings, else
    ``ValueError``. A missing acceptance file raises
    ``FileNotFoundError``; an invalid file -- including a version-1
    ``jobs.register`` file, which is never upgraded -- raises
    ``ValueError``; an unknown job id raises ``KeyError(job_id)``; any
    other locking or I/O failure raises ``OSError``. The call never
    writes, and the returned record is a fresh copy with job_id, work,
    deadline, regions, residency, max_cost, carbon_cap and state.
    """
    if not isinstance(path, str) or not path:
        raise ValueError("path must be a non-empty string")
    if not isinstance(job_id, str) or not job_id:
        raise ValueError("job_id must be a non-empty string")

    realpath = os.path.realpath(path)
    with _process_lock(realpath, shared=True):
        jobs, _idempotency, _events, raw = _load_submit_file(realpath)
    if raw is None:
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"acceptance file {realpath!r} does not exist")
    if job_id not in jobs:
        raise KeyError(job_id)
    return dict(jobs[job_id])

309	    # audit event: same-directory temporary, fsync, atomic replace and a

317	def publish(
318	    path: str,
319	    resource: dict[str, object],
320	    idempotency_key: str,
321	) -> tuple[dict[str, object], bool]:
322	    """Persistently publish one resource-supply version.
323	
324	    ``path`` and ``idempotency_key`` must be non-empty strings. The
325	    resource must be an object with exactly the eight top-level fields
326	    resource_id, region, capacity, start, end, unit_cost,
327	    carbon_intensity and residency: non-empty id and region strings, a
328	    positive integer capacity, non-negative start, end, unit_cost and
329	    carbon_intensity (booleans rejected) with start not later than end,
330	    and a non-empty residency list of distinct non-empty strings sorted
331	    by code point that contains the resource's own region. Any
332	    deviation raises ``ValueError`` before the file is touched.
333	
334	    A first publication saves the canonical record -- the resource
335	    fields plus the next consecutive ``version`` for that resource id,
336	    starting at 1 -- together with the idempotency binding and a
337	    publish audit event carrying the key, the resource id and the
338	    version, all three in one durable commit, and returns
339	    ``(record, True)``. A new version of an already published resource
340	    must carry a strictly later start than the current latest version.
341	    Replaying the same key with an identical resource returns the
342	    stored record with ``False`` without adding an event or rewriting
343	    the file; the same key with a different resource raises
344	    ``ValueError`` and preserves the original bytes.
345	
346	    A missing parent directory raises ``FileNotFoundError``; an invalid
347	    existing file (encoding, JSON, negative-zero or non-finite numbers,
348	    version, structure, ordering, canonical bytes or references) raises
349	    ``ValueError``; any other locking or I/O failure raises ``OSError``.
350	    Calls serialize across threads and processes per resolved real path.
351	    """
352	    if not isinstance(path, str) or not path:
353	        raise ValueError("path must be a non-empty string")
354	    if not isinstance(idempotency_key, str) or not idempotency_key:
355	        raise ValueError("idempotency_key must be a non-empty string")
356	    normalized = _normalize_resource(resource)
357	    resource_id = normalized["resource_id"]
358	
359	    store = _get_store(path)
360	    with store.lock:
361	        # Opening the companion lock in a missing directory surfaces as
362	        # FileNotFoundError before the data file is created.
363	        with _process_lock(store.realpath):
364	            history, idempotency, events, old_bytes = _load_file(
365	                store.realpath)
366	
367	            existing_id = idempotency.get(idempotency_key)
368	            if existing_id is not None:
369	                event = events[idempotency_key]
370	                existing = history[existing_id][event["version"] - 1]

def _fsync_directory(directory: str) -> None:
    _lifecycle.fsync_directory(directory)


def _rollback_file(realpath: str, directory: str,
                   old_bytes: bytes | None, first: BaseException) -> None:
    _lifecycle.rollback_file(realpath, directory, old_bytes, first,
                             prefix=".resources-restore-",
                             fsync_dir=_fsync_directory)


def _commit_file(realpath: str, payload: bytes,
                 old_bytes: bytes | None) -> None:
    # One durable commit for the history, the idempotency map and the
    # audit event: same-directory temporary, fsync, atomic replace and a
    # directory fsync. Any failure after the replace restores the
    # pre-call bytes, so an unsuccessful publish leaves the original file
    # byte-for-byte.
    _lifecycle.commit_file(realpath, payload, old_bytes,
                           prefix=".resources-", fsync_dir=_fsync_directory)


def publish(
    path: str,
    resource: dict[str, object],
    idempotency_key: str,
) -> tuple[dict[str, object], bool]:
    """Persistently publish one resource-supply version.

    ``path`` and ``idempotency_key`` must be non-empty strings. The
    resource must be an object with exactly the eight top-level fields
    resource_id, region, capacity, start, end, unit_cost,
    carbon_intensity and residency: non-empty id and region strings, a
    positive integer capacity, non-negative start, end, unit_cost and
    carbon_intensity (booleans rejected) with start not later than end,
    and a non-empty residency list of distinct non-empty strings sorted
    by code point that contains the resource's own region. Any
    deviation raises ``ValueError`` before the file is touched.

    A first publication saves the canonical record -- the resource
    fields plus the next consecutive ``version`` for that resource id,
    starting at 1 -- together with the idempotency binding and a
    publish audit event carrying the key, the resource id and the
    version, all three in one durable commit, and returns
    ``(record, True)``. A new version of an already published resource
    must carry a strictly later start than the current latest version.
    Replaying the same key with an identical resource returns the
    stored record with ``False`` without adding an event or rewriting
    the file; the same key with a different resource raises
    ``ValueError`` and preserves the original bytes.

    A missing parent directory raises ``FileNotFoundError``; an invalid
    existing file (encoding, JSON, negative-zero or non-finite numbers,
    version, structure, ordering, canonical bytes or references) raises
    ``ValueError``; any other locking or I/O failure raises ``OSError``.
    Calls serialize across threads and processes per resolved real path.
    """
    if not isinstance(path, str) or not path:
        raise ValueError("path must be a non-empty string")
    if not isinstance(idempotency_key, str) or not idempotency_key:
        raise ValueError("idempotency_key must be a non-empty string")
    normalized = _normalize_resource(resource)
    resource_id = normalized["resource_id"]

    store = _get_store(path)
    with store.lock:
        # Opening the companion lock in a missing directory surfaces as
        # FileNotFoundError before the data file is created.
        with _process_lock(store.realpath):
            history, idempotency, events, old_bytes = _load_file(
                store.realpath)

            existing_id = idempotency.get(idempotency_key)
            if existing_id is not None:
                event = events[idempotency_key]
                existing = history[existing_id][event["version"] - 1]
                if {field: existing[field]
                        for field in _RESOURCE_FIELDS} != normalized:
                    raise ValueError("idempotency key was already used with "
                                     "a different resource")
                return dict(existing), False

            versions = history.get(resource_id)
            if versions is None:
                versions = []
                history[resource_id] = versions
                version = 1
            else:
                if normalized["start"] <= versions[-1]["start"]:
                    raise ValueError("resource start must increase across "
                                     "versions")
                version = versions[-1]["version"] + 1

            record: dict[str, Any] = {
                "resource_id": resource_id,
                "version": version,
                "region": normalized["region"],
                "capacity": normalized["capacity"],
                "start": normalized["start"],
                "end": normalized["end"],
                "unit_cost": normalized["unit_cost"],
                "carbon_intensity": normalized["carbon_intensity"],
                "residency": list(normalized["residency"]),
            }
            versions.append(record)
            idempotency[idempotency_key] = resource_id
            events[idempotency_key] = {
                "key": idempotency_key,
                "resource_id": resource_id,
                "version": version,
            }
            _commit_file(store.realpath,
                         _serialize(history, idempotency, events), old_bytes)
            return dict(record), True

def _canonical_sections(
    sections: tuple[dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]], dict[str, str],
                    dict[str, dict[str, Any]]],
) -> bytes:
    history, idempotency, events = sections
    return _canonical_bytes(history, idempotency, events)


def _load_file(realpath: str) -> tuple[
    dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]], dict[str, str],
    dict[str, dict[str, Any]], bytes | None
]:
    # Every read entry requires the on-disk bytes to be the canonical
    # form: fields and keys in their original order, compact JSON with
    # non-ASCII written through and exactly one trailing newline. Any
    # extra whitespace, escaped non-ASCII character, reordered field or
    # missing/duplicated final newline is a ValueError. A missing file
    # maps to the empty initial state.
    sections, raw = _lifecycle.load_canonical(
        realpath, "supply file", _validate_structure, _canonical_sections)
    if sections is None:
        return {}, {}, {}, None
    history, idempotency, events = sections
    return history, idempotency, events, raw


def _serialize(
    history: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]],
    idempotency: dict[str, str],
    events: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
) -> bytes:
    # Compact UTF-8 JSON, non-ASCII written through, each section's
    # primary keys in code-point order, terminated by exactly one newline.
    payload = {
        "version": _VERSION,
        "history": {resource_id: history[resource_id]
                    for resource_id in sorted(history)},
        "idempotency": {key: idempotency[key] for key in sorted(idempotency)},
        "audit": {key: events[key] for key in sorted(events)},
    }
    text = json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"),
                      allow_nan=False) + "\n"
    return text.encode("utf-8")

    """Match a registered job to the greenest feasible offer idempotently.

    Candidates are offers whose region is permitted by the job's
    residency_regions and whose remaining capacity (capacity_wh minus the
    energy already allocated in the ledger) covers the job's energy_wh;
    the winner is the first by ascending carbon_intensity, unit_cost and
    resource_id. Returns ``(record, created)`` where ``record`` carries
    job_id and resource_id; ``created`` is ``True`` for a new match and
    ``False`` when the idempotency key replays a match for the same job
    (which allocates no further capacity).
    """
    for value in (jobs, offers, ledger, job_id, key):
        if not isinstance(value, str) or not value:
            raise ValueError("jobs, offers, ledger, job_id and key must be "
                             "non-empty strings")

    store = _get_store(ledger)
    with store.lock:
        job_records, _ = _load_registry(
            os.path.realpath(jobs), _jobs._validate_structure, "jobs registry")
        if job_id not in job_records:
            raise KeyError(job_id)
        job = job_records[job_id]

        offer_records, _ = _load_registry(
            os.path.realpath(offers), _offers._validate_structure,
            "offers registry")
        matches, idempotency = _load_ledger(
            store.realpath, job_records, offer_records)

        existing = idempotency.get(key)
        if existing is not None:
            if existing != job_id:
                raise ValueError("idempotency key was already used with a "
                                 "different job")
            return dict(matches[job_id]), False
        if job_id in matches:
            raise ValueError("job is already matched under another "
                             "idempotency key")

        allocated: dict[str, int] = {}
        for record in matches.values():
            resource_id = record["resource_id"]
            allocated[resource_id] = (
                allocated.get(resource_id, 0)
                + job_records[record["job_id"]]["energy_wh"])

        allowed = set(job["residency_regions"])
        needed = job["energy_wh"]
        best: tuple[int, int, str] | None = None
        for resource_id, offer in offer_records.items():
            if offer["region"] not in allowed:

                         resource_id)

        matches[job_id] = record
        idempotency[key] = job_id

1	"""Cross-process concurrency tests for the persistent market ledgers.
2	
3	The sibling thread-based tests (``test_completion_concurrency.py`` and
4	``test_migration_consumer_concurrency.py``) prove the in-process mutex
5	registry; these tests prove the companion ``flock`` file locks carry
6	the same guarantees across operating-system processes. Two independent
7	interpreter processes -- started with the ``spawn`` method so no lock,
8	store registry or module state is inherited -- race the existing public
9	entry points ``cancellation.cancel``, ``dispatch.commit``,
10	``market.clear`` and ``market.clear_live`` over one shared set of
11	ledger files, staged at deterministic synchronization points (events,
12	barriers and lock-attempt probes installed inside each child) instead
13	of fixed sleeps.
14	
15	Two race families are covered:
16	
17	* the first cancellation of a traded job versus its first dispatch
18	  commit -- exactly one side commits with ``created`` true; a committed
19	  cancellation makes the commit fail with ``ValueError``, a committed
20	  dispatch decision makes the cancellation fail with
21	  ``PermissionError``, and the loser leaves no record, no temporary
22	  fragment and no damage to the winner's commit;
23	* the cancellation of a job that exactly fills a resource version
24	  versus the clearing of a new job against the same version -- a
25	  clearing that snapshots first is refused with ``LookupError`` and
26	  succeeds on retry once the cancellation lands, a clearing that
27	  snapshots after the cancellation books the released capacity
28	  directly, and the effective occupancy never exceeds the capacity of
29	  the resource version.
30	
31	Every child reports its return value or exception type through a queue
32	and is joined with a bounded wait; a stuck child is terminated so a
33	deadlock surfaces as a loud test failure instead of a hang. All
34	verification goes through the public read/replay entries and the
35	on-disk bytes. No interface, ledger format, exception type or
36	sequential-call result is changed, and the existing thread-based tests
37	keep their assertions untouched.
38	"""
39

41

43	import multiprocessing as mp
44	import os

46	import unittest

104	# -- child-process machinery -------------------------------------------------
105	#
106	# The workers below run inside the spawned child interpreters; they must
107	# stay module-level so the spawn pickler can resolve them by name. Each
108	# worker optionally installs a gate (holding the child's business call at
109	# a deterministic point while it keeps every lock it already holds) or a
110	# lock-attempt probe (only observing), then runs exactly one public entry
111	# point and reports the outcome as one small picklable dict.

114	def _child_report(queue, fn) -> None:
115	    """Run ``fn`` and report the outcome; the child exits 0 unless it
116	    crashes outside the business call."""
117	    try:
118	        record, created = fn()
119	    except BaseException as exc:
120	        queue.put({"status": "raised", "exc_type": type(exc).__name__,
121	                   "message": str(exc)})
122	    else:
123	        queue.put({"status": "returned", "record": record,
124	                   "created": created})

127	def _gate_commit_file(module, arrived, release) -> None:
128	    """Hold the module's atomic commit until the parent opens the gate:
129	    the child keeps every lock it already holds while the rival process
130	    is staged behind it."""
131	    real_commit = module._commit_file
132	
133	    def gated_commit(realpath, payload, old_bytes):
134	        arrived.set()
135	        if not release.wait(_WAIT):
136	            raise RuntimeError("test gate was never released")
137	        return real_commit(realpath, payload, old_bytes)
138	
139	    module._commit_file = gated_commit

143	    """Hold ``market.clear``/``clear_live`` just before the clearing
144	    ledger is loaded -- after the cancellation snapshot was read and
145	    while every lock is held -- until the parent opens the gate."""
146	    real_load = market_module._load_clear_ledger
147	    fired = {"done": False}
148	
149	    def gated_load(*args, **kwargs):
150	        if not fired["done"]:
151	            fired["done"] = True
152	            arrived.set()
153	            if not release.wait(_WAIT):
154	                raise RuntimeError("test gate was never released")
155	        return real_load(*args, **kwargs)

157	    market_module._load_clear_ledger = gated_load

161	    """Signal the parent when the child is about to block on
162	    ``probe_realpath``'s flock; the probe only observes and never
163	    changes the underlying lock behavior."""
164	    real_lock = getattr(module, attribute)
165	
166	    @contextlib.contextmanager
167	    def probed(realpath, *, shared=False):
168	        if realpath == probe_realpath:
169	            probing.set()
170	        with real_lock(realpath, shared=shared):
171	            yield
172	
173	    setattr(module, attribute, probed)

215	class _ProcessRaceTestBase(unittest.TestCase):
216	    """Shared paths, spawn harness and report assertions."""
217	
218	    def setUp(self) -> None:
219	        self.tmp = TemporaryDirectory()
220	        self.addCleanup(self.tmp.cleanup)
221	        base = self.tmp.name
222	        self.jobs = os.path.join(base, "jobs.json")
223	        self.supply = os.path.join(base, "supply.json")
224	        self.signals = os.path.join(base, "signals.json")
225	        self.trades = os.path.join(base, "trades.json")
226	        self.dispatch = os.path.join(base, "dispatch.json")
227	        self.cancellations = os.path.join(base, "cancellations.json")
228	        # Spawned children inherit neither the in-process store registry
229	        # nor any lock state: only the on-disk flock files serialize them.
230	        self._ctx = mp.get_context("spawn")
231	        self._children: list[tuple[mp.Process, object]] = []
232	        self.addCleanup(self._terminate_children)
233	
234	    # -- process harness ---------------------------------------------------
235	
236	    def _terminate_children(self) -> None:
237	        for proc, _queue in self._children:
238	            if proc.is_alive():
239	                proc.terminate()
240	                proc.join(_WAIT)
241	
242	    def _event(self):
243	        return self._ctx.Event()
244	
245	    def _spawn(self, target, args):
246	        queue = self._ctx.Queue()
247	        proc = self._ctx.Process(target=target, args=(*args, queue),
248	                                 daemon=True)
249	        proc.start()
250	        self._children.append((proc, queue))
251	        return proc, queue

253	    def _await_event(self, event, label: str) -> None:
254	        self.assertTrue(event.wait(_WAIT),
255	                        f"timed out waiting for {label}")
256	
257	    def _finish(self, proc, queue, label: str):
258	        """Join one child with a bounded wait and collect its exit
259	        status and report; a stuck child is terminated so a deadlock
260	        fails loudly instead of hanging."""
261	        proc.join(_WAIT)
262	        if proc.is_alive():
263	            proc.terminate()
264	            proc.join(_WAIT)
265	            self.fail(f"{label} did not finish within {_WAIT} seconds "
266	                      "(possible deadlock)")
267	        self.assertEqual(proc.exitcode, 0,
268	                         f"{label} exited with status {proc.exitcode}")
269	        try:
270	            report = queue.get(timeout=_WAIT)
271	        except queue_module.Empty:
272	            self.fail(f"{label} left no report")
273	        queue.close()
274	        return report
